Bob Hewitt Trial

By: Este de Klerk | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Four years after the story broke that former Grand Slam doubles champion Bob Hewitt allegedly raped and sexually assaulted girls he coached in SA decades ago, he's now standing trial on the charges.

Summary:
Four years after the story broke that former Grand Slam doubles champion and one-time Tennis Hall of Famer Bob Hewitt allegedly raped and sexually assaulted girls he coached in SA decades ago, he'll be standing trial in the South Gauteng High Court in Johannesburg from 9 to 20 February on two charges of rape and one of sexual assault.

Further information:
Hewitt was charged in 2013, but the indictment was only served on him in June 2014. At the time, he wasn't asked to enter a plea, but his attorney, Alwyn Griebenow indicated Hewitt will plead not guilty to all charges.

Hewitt is accused of raping Twiggy Tolken - then under the age of 16 - in 1981, raping Suellen Sheehan - then under the age of 16 - in 1982, and sexually assaulting Amanda Weinhold in 1994, when she was 16.

The 1981 alleged offence is said to have occured two years after Hewitt won the last of his 15 Grand Slam doubles and mixed doubled titles. Two of the alleged offences are said to have occured in the city of Boksburg, east of Johannesburg, and one in the Sun City casino resort.

At least one other woman in the United States has accused Hewitt of sexually abusing her when she was a minor.

The Australian-born Hewitt won nine Grand Slam doubles and six mixed doubles titles in the 1960s and 1970s, playing occasionally with former stars Arthur Ashe and Billie Jean King. He also reached the semi-finals of the mens's singles at the Australian Ope three times and won the Davis Cup with South Africa in 1974 after moving here.

Hewitt was inducted into the Rhode Island-based Tennis Hall of Fame in 1992 as a master of the doubles craft. He was indefinitely suspended from the hall in 2012 and his legacy stripped from the institution after an investigation into the allegations of sexual abuse, during which he was interviewed by attorneys hired by the hall.

Hewitt missed earlier court dates in Boksburg citing ill health, but pitched for his court appearance in June last year when the indictment was read out to him. He arrived at court using a walking stick. Hewitt's attorney presented a report from his doctor in 2013, as a court document, stating that Hewitt had a stroke in 2010, a heart attack in 2011 and suffered from anxiety attacks and depression among other health problems.

The charges against Hewitt stem from allegations, uncovered in a 2011 Globe newspaper investigation, that Hewitt sexually abused underage girls he coached, from Greater Boston to South Africa, from the 1970s to 1990s. The review was set in motion by Heather Browe Conner, a teacher at Reading Memorial High School, who said Hewitt raped her when she was a 15-year old student at Masconomet Regional High School. Conner has been frustrated in seeking charges against Hewitt in Massachusetts, but has supported the alleged victims in South Africa.

Press Release:



Bob Hewitt on Trial
This week former Grand Slam doubles tennis champion Bob Hewitt pleaded not guilty to two charges of rape and one of sexual assault against girls he coached in South Africa decades ago. Carte Blanche investigates the history of the allegations as the eyes of the world turn once again to the South African justice system.


Script:


BOB HEWITT TRIAL SCRIPT

PRODUCER: ESTé DE KLERK

DEREK LINK: He was the double star of the era, winning all the Grand Slams and filling seats at stadiums around the world.

[NAT SOUND]

DEREK LINK: This week he is filling benches here at the Palm Ridge High Court, the focus is still on tennis, but on crimes he allegedly committed off the court.

Hewitt, now 75, is no longer the shining young sport star of yesteryear…

He stands trial on two charges of rape and one of sexual assault.

JUDGE BERT BAM: Yes, mr. Hewitt, how do you plead?

BOB HEWITT: I plead not guilty, My Lord.

In Hewitt’s plea explanation, he said: “No matter what happens here, my life as I once knew it, is over.”

His alleged victims say their lives are also forever changed.

SUELLEN SHEEHAN: He had a horrible habit of standing up behind me and I would feel his erect penis in the small of my back.

Suellen Sheehan was the first South African to lay criminal charges against Hewitt. Twiggy Tolken, now living in New Zealand, and a third alleged victim who didn’t want to be named, followed.

SUELLEN SHEEHAN: He fetched me from school one Tuesday afternoon, took me to tennis and saw an opportunity and it happened.

Hewitt emphatically denied all the allegations against him.
On Thursday, his legal team argued that the state had insufficient evidence for a case, but Judge Bert Bum dismissed this application and Hewitt was called to the stand. Hewitt testified he did not have sexual intercourse with any of his alleged victims.

HEATHER CROWE CONNOR: I was sexually abused by my tennis coach from the age of 14 to 28.

In 2011, Heather Crowe Connor from Massachusetts became the first of Hewitt’s former students to voice allegations of rape and sexual abuse. She alleges she was 14 when Hewitt first raped her.

HEATHER CROWE CONNOR: Having dreams ruined and crushed, and feeling that you are ruined for life.

DEREK: Heather, when was the first time that you had intercourse with Bob Hewitt?

HEATHER CROWE CONNOR: The plan was I was going to babysit his daughter, and then when they got back, he was going to drive me home. He asked me to find a place between his hotel and my house.

DEREK: Do you feel that you were raped?

HEATHER CROW CONNOR: Yes, because I had no idea what was happening and I didn’t think I had any other choice.

In a 2012 radio interview Hewitt denied Heather’s allegations.

BOB HEWITT: She’s made some accusations, but they’re unfounded and I don’t know why she would like to raise this issue so late. She says, well, you know, we had a twelve-year relationship. She must have been out here, because this is where I was most of those twelve years.

Heather’s story led to an international investigation by Boston Globe newspaper journalist, Bob Hohler.

BOB HOHLER: We suspected that it’s not only one victim, that there may be other victims. Heather didn’t know of any other victims. She is really the unsung heroes in this whole thing. She had the courage to come forward and give her name and identify the person who’d abused her.

Hohler found several other alleged victims, including the three South Africans who took Hewitt to court. All told stories of alleged sexual abuse by their trusted coach.

BOB HEWITT: Some women climbed in on the bandwagon with this and you can’t defend this.

Twiggy Tolken has accused Hewitt of sexually assaulting and raping her when she was 13.
She testified that he allegedly forced her to perform oral sex in the car on the way to a training trip at Sun City in 1980.
She said that while in his hotel room, he told her to take off her clothes, and lie on top of him in the bath. She told the court: “I was brought up to do as I was told.” After that, he allegedly raped her on the bed. When she told him that it hurt, he said: “I’ll try again later.”

When she told her parents, they laid criminal charges, but Hewitt was never prosecuted.

Hewitt denied Twiggy’s allegations, testifying she was never alone - or with him in a room at Sun City.
Under cross-examination, Hewitt said: “If I had sex with Tolken, she would’ve had to go to the hospital straight. I can assure you.
“If she pulled down her panties, how can the state say there was no consent?”

He said he’d always had respectful relationships with the alleged victims. But former South African tennis player, Ray Moore who knew him well, says Hewitt had a reputation for spending time with young girls.

RAY MOORE: It was always - there is Bob again, sitting up in the stand with a young girl, and that happened many, many times, but no one even imagine that it went further than that.

Despite these allegations, Hewitt’s loyal wife of 50 years, Delaille, has remained at his side.

DEREK: You say that you have been threatened possibly by Bob’s wife?

SUELLEN: I have no doubt it was her.

VOICE MESSAGE: “You stupid Bitch. Are you still looking for drug money? You’re starting the whole thing up again, huh? We’re watching you. We know where your son is. We know where you are.”

Delaille Hewitt admitted to making the call. In a legal letter, she states: “The call was made after numerous publications on Mrs Sheehan’s facebook referring to Mr Hewitt as a paedophile, a child molester and a pervert.”

Suellen admitted to sharing a petition link in 2011, in which Hewitt was referred to as a paedophile.

DEREK: Apart from the one time you claim he had raped you, how many times have you had intercourse?

SUELLEN SHEEHAN: That was the only time we had intercourse. I performed oral sex on him, and him looking down my panties and touching my breasts.

In Hewitt’s testimony he denied all Suellen’s allegations and said that her parents, brother and ex-husband support him and say she’s a pathological liar.

SUELLEN: That’s their opinion. My mom has never really ever supported me very much. She actually asked me if I was pregnant and it came out in 2011: ‘The reason why I asked you is because I knew you and Bob were sleeping together.”

Hewitt’s third alleged victim accused him of sexually assaulting her for three years in the early 90s – a claim Hewitt has also denied.

His legal team repeatedly asked the women whether they ever refused his alleged advances.

HEATHER: I don’t really know how a young girl can really resist a six-foot-four, two-hundred plus pound man, let alone somebody that they look up to.

SUELLEN SHEEHAN: I didn’t resist him, I trusted him. He had told me that this was something we needed to do.

Clinical psychologist, dr Dorianne Weil, says that if the allegations are true, it’s likely that his alleged victims were in awe of his celebrity status.

DORIANNE WEIL: There is a seduction aspect of it, a wish to really, really be recognised at all costs. Sometimes, as far as the students are concerned, they feel that they have some status by having a celebrity as a teacher.

SUELLEN SHEEHAN: I thought I was very special to him and I was probably the only one, in my mind this famous icon shared something with me

DORIANNE WEIL: Even if there’s some sort of lack of protest from a young person, it is still up to the adult person to control themselves and their urges or their desires.

Twiggy testified Hewitt often told her he loved her. Three letters he’d written her, were handed in as evidence.
One reads: “From: Your love; To: My little and big love. I’m cross with you for not trusting me. I can only assume you think of me as a sex maniac.”

In response, Hewitt testified that at Sun City, he taught show-girls to play tennis and Twiggy therefore referred to him as a sex maniac.

In another letter, he wrote: “You are really the only person capable of lifting me up… I’m always available in body, heart and mind, as well as soul.”

Hewitt admitted the letters were inappropriate, but they were innocent and in response to letters Twiggy wrote him.

DEREK LINK: A string of tennis officials and promoters have told us around the 70s and 80s there were many questions about Bob Hewitt’s behaviour around young girls. He was taken off certain coaching duties.

DEREK: What did the South African Tennis Union know about Bob’s behaviour?

RAY MOORE: I learned that reports had been filed to three different Presidents. All three had the same philosophy and that was there wasn’t anything they could do legally until official charges were filed.

DEREK: Would you call it a cover-up?

RAY MOORE: No, not at all. I think it was a case of kicking the can down the road.

The International Tennis Hall of Fame indefinitely suspended Hewitt in 2012.

RAY MOORE: The 26 members on the board of the Tennis Hall of Fame, they voted unanimously to throw Hewitt out of the Tennis Hall of Fame.

DEREK: Do you think you could have done more yourself?

RAY MOORE: I sometimes scold myself for not having done more. Hearing their stories, there comes a time where you have to take a position, I had to do that and they had to do that.

DEREK LINK: In recent years headlines have been filled with celebrities who’ve been found guilty of raping or sexually assaulting young girls many decades earlier. And the recent allegations against Prince Andrew and Bill Cosby are actually mentioned in Bob Hewitt’s plea explanation.

Hewitt states: “There appears to be an attitude that where a young lady lays a charge, it must be true. Prince Andrew and Bill Cosby are the latest victims of the wild and belated allegations of sexual impropriety. In my case, it is not true and I strongly dispute it.”

The time period for Heather to lay criminal charges against Hewitt in the United States has passed the statute of limitations.
But she’s pursuing a civil case and Hewitt’s been served with papers.

HEATHER: Dealing with your conscience isn’t quite enough when you’ve damaged people, so I feel, you know, it should be a life sentence.

We know where your son is. We know where you are.” Delaille Hewitt admitted to making the call. In a legal letter, she states: “The call was made after numerous publications on Mrs Sheehan’s facebook referring to Mr Hewitt as a paedophile, a child molester and a pervert.” Suellen admitted to sharing a petition link in 2011, in which Hewitt was referred to as a paedophile. DEREK: Apart from the one time you claim he had raped you, how many times have you had intercourse? SUELLEN SHEEHAN: That was the only time we had intercourse. I performed oral sex on him, and him looking down my panties and touching my breasts. In Hewitt’s testimony he denied all Suellen’s allegations and said that her parents, brother and ex-husband support him and say she’s a pathological liar. SUELLEN: That’s their opinion. My mom has never really ever supported me very much. She actually asked me if I was pregnant and it came out in 2011: ‘The reason why I asked you is because I knew you and Bob were sleeping together.” Hewitt’s third alleged victim accused him of sexually assaulting her for three years in the early 90s – a claim Hewitt has also denied. His legal team repeatedly asked the women whether they ever refused his alleged advances. HEATHER: I don’t really know how a young girl can really resist a six-foot-four, two-hundred plus pound man, let alone somebody that they look up to. SUELLEN SHEEHAN: I didn’t resist him, I trusted him. He had told me that this was something we needed to do. Clinical psychologist, dr Dorianne Weil, says that if the allegations are true, it’s likely that his alleged victims were in awe of his celebrity status. DORIANNE WEIL: There is a seduction aspect of it, a wish to really, really be recognised at all costs. Sometimes, as far as the students are concerned, they feel that they have some status by having a celebrity as a teacher. SUELLEN SHEEHAN: I thought I was very special to him and I was probably the only one, in my mind this famous icon shared something with me DORIANNE WEIL: Even if there’s some sort of lack of protest from a young person, it is still up to the adult person to control themselves and their urges or their desires. Twiggy testified Hewitt often told her he loved her. Three letters he’d written her, were handed in as evidence. One reads: “From: Your love; To: My little and big love. I’m cross with you for not trusting me. I can only assume you think of me as a sex maniac.” In response, Hewitt testified that at Sun City, he taught show-girls to play tennis and Twiggy therefore referred to him as a sex maniac. In another letter, he wrote: “You are really the only person capable of lifting me up… I’m always available in body, heart and mind, as well as soul.” Hewitt admitted the letters were inappropriate, but they were innocent and in response to letters Twiggy wrote him. DEREK LINK: A string of tennis officials and promoters have told us around the 70s and 80s there were many questions about Bob Hewitt’s behaviour around young girls. He was taken off certain coaching duties. DEREK: What did the South African Tennis Union know about Bob’s behaviour? RAY MOORE: I learned that reports had been filed to three different Presidents. All three had the same philosophy and that was there wasn’t anything they could do legally until official charges were filed. DEREK: Would you call it a cover-up? RAY MOORE: No, not at all. I think it was a case of kicking the can down the road. The International Tennis Hall of Fame indefinitely suspended Hewitt in 2012. RAY MOORE: The 26 members on the board of the Tennis Hall of Fame, they voted unanimously to throw Hewitt out of the Tennis Hall of Fame. DEREK: Do you think you could have done more yourself? RAY MOORE: I sometimes scold myself for not having done more. Hearing their stories, there comes a time where you have to take a position, I had to do that and they had to do that. DEREK LINK: In recent years headlines have been filled with celebrities who’ve been found guilty of raping or sexually assaulting young girls many decades earlier. And the recent allegations against Prince Andrew and Bill Cosby are actually mentioned in Bob Hewitt’s plea explanation. Hewitt states: “There appears to be an attitude that where a young lady lays a charge, it must be true. Prince Andrew and Bill Cosby are the latest victims of the wild and belated allegations of sexual impropriety. In my case, it is not true and I strongly dispute it.” The time period for Heather to lay criminal charges against Hewitt in the United States has passed the statute of limitations. But she’s pursuing a civil case and Hewitt’s been served with papers. HEATHER: Dealing with your conscience isn’t quite enough when you’ve damaged people, so I feel, you know, it should be a life sentence. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Four years after the story broke that former Grand Slam doubles champion Bob Hewitt allegedly raped and sexually assaulted girls he coached in SA decades ago, he's now standing trial on the charges.
metadata.Summary: Four years after the story broke that former Grand Slam doubles champion and one-time Tennis Hall of Famer Bob Hewitt allegedly raped and sexually assaulted girls he coached in SA decades ago, he'll be standing trial in the South Gauteng High Court in Johannesburg from 9 to 20 February on two charges of rape and one of sexual assault.
metadata.Further information: Hewitt was charged in 2013, but the indictment was only served on him in June 2014. At the time, he wasn't asked to enter a plea, but his attorney, Alwyn Griebenow indicated Hewitt will plead not guilty to all charges. Hewitt is accused of raping Twiggy Tolken - then under the age of 16 - in 1981, raping Suellen Sheehan - then under the age of 16 - in 1982, and sexually assaulting Amanda Weinhold in 1994, when she was 16. The 1981 alleged offence is said to have occured two years after Hewitt won the last of his 15 Grand Slam doubles and mixed doubled titles. Two of the alleged offences are said to have occured in the city of Boksburg, east of Johannesburg, and one in the Sun City casino resort. At least one other woman in the United States has accused Hewitt of sexually abusing her when she was a minor. The Australian-born Hewitt won nine Grand Slam doubles and six mixed doubles titles in the 1960s and 1970s, playing occasionally with former stars Arthur Ashe and Billie Jean King. He also reached the semi-finals of the mens's singles at the Australian Ope three times and won the Davis Cup with South Africa in 1974 after moving here. Hewitt was inducted into the Rhode Island-based Tennis Hall of Fame in 1992 as a master of the doubles craft. He was indefinitely suspended from the hall in 2012 and his legacy stripped from the institution after an investigation into the allegations of sexual abuse, during which he was interviewed by attorneys hired by the hall. Hewitt missed earlier court dates in Boksburg citing ill health, but pitched for his court appearance in June last year when the indictment was read out to him. He arrived at court using a walking stick. Hewitt's attorney presented a report from his doctor in 2013, as a court document, stating that Hewitt had a stroke in 2010, a heart attack in 2011 and suffered from anxiety attacks and depression among other health problems. The charges against Hewitt stem from allegations, uncovered in a 2011 Globe newspaper investigation, that Hewitt sexually abused underage girls he coached, from Greater Boston to South Africa, from the 1970s to 1990s. The review was set in motion by Heather Browe Conner, a teacher at Reading Memorial High School, who said Hewitt raped her when she was a 15-year old student at Masconomet Regional High School. Conner has been frustrated in seeking charges against Hewitt in Massachusetts, but has supported the alleged victims in South Africa.
